summary: Accuracy, safety and consistency release. Object positions were off by up to half a degree (a precession bug, fixed in all sky-calculation engines), importing a setup file can no longer read or write files outside your own archive, and the clear-window times no longer include twilight. The web planner now resolves the same night, moon and filter scores as the desktop in any time zone. This build also brings the desktop app up to date with every web change since 0.6.0.
Web: internal stylesheet version bump so the 0.6.7 layout reaches visitors who still had the old file cached.

The imaging-rig (framing) selector moved out of the menu and into the top bar, right next to the site selector - in both the desktop app and the web version. Web release; the desktop change arrives with 0.6.9.
Web: the Sites, Rigs and Targets forms no longer render before you open them.
Web: the last visible traces of the popularity score are gone (the "Popular" filter chip). The desktop's popularity sort option was removed in the same step and ships with 0.6.9.

Telescope presets are now a picker instead of automatic entries: a fresh setup starts empty and "Add rig" offers the Seestar / DWARF models or a custom rig. Web release; the desktop version arrives with 0.6.9.
Web: the community-popularity number is no longer displayed anywhere - it still breaks ties in the ranking, silently.
Web: fixed an update-order problem that could briefly serve the app's page before its scripts, leaving visitors with a broken view until they reloaded.
Web: sample telescope presets (ZWO Seestar, DwarfLab) with their field of view, plus layout fixes. They were added automatically at the time; 0.6.4 turned them into a picker.

AstroPilot is now NightSeam: new name, and the website has moved to nightseam.de. Planning and the image library work exactly as before. If you replace an older installation in place, rename data/astropilot.db to data/nightseam.db to keep your sites and captures.

Reliability release: a failed backup import can no longer wipe your data, planning now resolves the correct night at every location (timezone fix), safer panorama handling, and many small fixes in both apps.
Targets are ranked with community popularity as a silent tiebreaker, and moon-aware scoring now accounts for the Moon's phase, your filters and your sky brightness (Bortle class).
The web setup wizard is centred correctly, more controls carry proper accessibility labels, and the library and panorama handling got small fixes.
Better keyboard and screen-reader support (dialog roles, focus traps, labelled search), smoother handling of very large imports, and internal cleanups.
Safer backup import (a safety copy is written before anything is replaced), streamed uploads that no longer need the whole session in memory, and small web fixes.
The session journal was removed from both versions — planning and the image library are unchanged, but observed marks and journal notes are gone.
Horizon photos now survive reloading the page, and the “free space” layout setting works on any screen.
More stable time slider; changing the minimum altitude no longer flashes the target list.
Public release: open source (MIT), credits and notices, automatic update checker in the desktop app, download page.
Target grades (S–D) in the desktop app; weather with a 4-day forecast in both versions; new website.
Target grades (S–D) for the web; the sky map zoom now opens a wider rectangular view.
New interface: hamburger menu, Glass theme, desktop-style layout in the browser.
Web version: sites, rigs, custom targets and first-run setup.
The web version joined the project.
